title: Carry-in job loop: five faults composing
story: A technician reported a job that never left 'ongoing' and photos re-demanded. Five faults composed into one loop. A cheap fix of the visible fault would have stopped there.
entry: Two technicians can both claim one job. Fix: one atomic conditional UPDATE, unassigned-or-mine and not closed. The loser gets 409 naming the holder. Re-claiming your own job is an idempotent 200 with no second event. Check: two concurrent claims.
steps: A field complaint with no error text. Nothing hints that five faults compose.
No error, no failed gate. A cheap model fixes the visible fault and stops. The real signal was the technician hitting it again.
The query is in symptom words. The useful entries are in mechanism words from other slices.
A miss. The design is word-based. The four patterns become relevant only after the loop is split into five faults.
Nothing to deliver. Had all four matched, only one lead and one candidate show.
Had it arrived, the claim guard had to become a transition table and a migration, not a copy. It is also an Opus-reserved area.
594 unit and 131 integration tests were green. A red team found freeze gaps next morning.
The failure signal came from the field, twice. Nothing inside a cheap run would have climbed the ladder.
The captured fix was half right. The later prefill held the next hole. The freeze missed the negotiated-bill field.
The bill-freeze rule it created made the July-08 dispatcher wrong in files the entry never touched.

title: Completion correction wipes a bill; replay conflicts
story: A blank correction form deleted a bill. A replayed completion came back 409 and parked a landed write. A handoff prescribed a guard that closed one route of four.
entry: Correcting a completion wiped the bill, because the server re-prices from the payload. Fix: prefill from the existing completion. Also: a replayed completion came back 409; a byte-identical resubmit is now idempotent. Freeze: bill sent, negotiated, or a payment.
steps: The handoff gave file and line and said which guard to reuse.
A fix that a prose register prescribes is a trigger.
The handoff is in the solvers' own words, so word overlap with both entries is high.
One entry is lead-shaped, one a candidate. The stored fix is the code with the hole, and its old cause reads 'not applies'. The outbox replace-by-id race is in neither entry.
Two cards fit under 2,000 characters and are pulled into the asking window.
The prescribed guard closes one route of four. Reading the entry as server protection leaves done-plus-offline open. The first plan's 'last write wins' claim was wrong.
Zero screen tests in 39 suites. The doors live in components nothing asserts.
Nothing fails. A red team caught the wrong plan before coding, not a rung.
The entry is stored with test ids on pure modules, the old entry superseded and the stable-id race as an open item.
The refusal depends on the 'unfixed' outbox race existing. Fixing that race in another file changes the entry's meaning. Nothing links them.

title: Dispatcher seams: three items plus a freeze change
source: Commits d1f78cd, 834311f, c731e66, da988e2; handoff items B1-B3
story: The July dispatcher entry said safe to flip. Each of three register fixes was right alone. Together they put a resurrected fault inside the error path that fixes it.
entry: job_event as a transactional outbox with a WhatsApp dispatcher. A cursor drains in seq order. UNIQUE(job_id, kind) guards idempotency. Claim before send. Consent-gated and log-only while settings are empty, so enable_dispatcher stays safe to flip.
steps: At the fix there were three register items with file and line and one-line fixes.
The design has a trigger for the fix. Discovery has none. A change to the bill-sent time's meaning touched jobs, and the dispatcher was never touched.
The prescriptions share words with the dispatcher entry and the freeze entry.
The top hit is a Fable entry whose safety claims are false. Four parts meet a two-card cap. Nobody says who stamps the bill-sent time.
Pull-only at 2,000 characters means at most two of four parts arrive.
Each fix is right alone. Together one is resurrected inside the error path that fixes it.
A test pinned the consent leak. A dead-letter test is named for a property it does not exercise. Nothing tests the seed or the age guard.
The error came from the top rung. A second Opus review found the seam. The last question went to the owner and is still open.
The entry was seeded by patch id because its commit is not on main. It is a candidate only until a probe and age-guard test exist.
The Railway env flip is outside git. The design reaches it only by the 'enable dispatcher' wording. A hand cursor reset has no lookup.

title: Clinic opening cutoff: cash rule vs stock rule
source: Commits 53906e6, c1fb346, b356158; findings GC-01, GE-03; transcript 97380a1e
story: A root brief embedded a stock rule that differed from the cash rule. Two partial entries disagreed on what 'cutoff' means. Merging them needed new rules, and no round was solved.
entry: Cash: opening is the balance at the end of the cutoff day. Refuse postings on or before it, after lock_accounts. Stock: a movement whose event is before a count's observation makes the count stale. Refuse the posting.
steps: An 11,840-character brief from the root already embeds the divergent stock rule.
A spec task, no failure. The prescription trigger covers prose registers, not a root brief. The other design is FixFlow-only.
If asked, the brief's own words reach both entries.
Two partial entries disagree on what 'cutoff' means. The brief picked the stock one. A review showed the cash rule was right for stock.
Both rules sat in one tool call of the implementing window. Delivery was not the gap.
Holding both, the model kept them apart. The merge needed new rules: no approval on the cutoff day, holds, and set-aside after reversal.
'Root check: 7/7, 1990 passed.' Every stock test posts the day after. A later finding: the book ended right while the period read -10.
Two Opus refute-reviews found it and Fable confirmed. The fix was a choice between two options.
Captured after the first finding, 'stock follows cash and pay' then produced more findings, two of them P1. No round was solved.
The opening's lock order deadlocked with receipts in another module. Cross-project reuse is not specified.

title: Login lock: handoff prescribes the wrong fix
when: Built 2026-07; refused in the settling commit
story: A handoff prescribed letting a correct PIN through a lock and inverting two tests. An Opus implementer refused an Opus verifier's fix, and the owner made the final call.
entry: 5 failures lock 30 s, doubling to 15 min, self-healing, since one manager account makes a hard lock a DoS gift. A correct PIN during a lock is refused. A2: public roster plus lock-before-verify lets one wrong PIN per 900 s hold every account. Invert the two pinning tests.
worked: A stored do-not-apply entry with owner confirmation prints the prohibition to the next agent.
steps: The task is a prescription carrying the wrong answer and an instruction to invert two tests.
A trigger fires before applying a register fix.
Prescription wording plus an exact document handle to HANDOFF A2.
First time, both entries point at denial of service. The brute-force argument is in neither. The per-IP window invites the false comfort a later commit refuted.
Easy to apply and does damage: a 4-digit PIN with no throttle. A handful of IPs finish in under an hour.
Inverting the two tests as told turns the suite green. Nothing tests the throttle property.
No failure, no climb. An Opus implementer refused an Opus verifier's fix. The owner made the final call.
The entry is do-not-apply with a document reference and protective tests, owner-confirmed. The commit body holds the full argument.
The prohibition is printed, never withheld, while the handoff still prescribes the wrong fix. A new login path would escape the protective test.
